attributes.body_ja:
「にしては」は、「(A) を考（かんが）えると (B) だ」や「(A) であり (B) でもある」を表（あらわ）しますが、「は」が副助詞（ふくじょし）の「も」に変（か）わった「にしても」は、(B) により強調（きょうちょう）が加（くわ）わった表現（ひょうげん）になります。

「にしても」は、普通形（ふつうけい）の語（ご）に付（つ）いて、「(A) であることを考（かんが）えても、(B) だ」や「もし (A) だったとしても、(B) だ」のような意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。「にして」は、複数（ふくすう）の要素（ようそ）からできていますが、一（ひと）つの副助詞（ふくじょし）だと考（かんが）えられています。

「にしても」は、「どこ」「どの」「だれ」「なに」のような疑問詞（ぎもんし）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われることも多（おお）いです。この場合（ばあい）、「(A) がはっきり決（き）まっていなくても (B) だ」という意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「にしても」は、(A) と (B) が同時（どうじ）に成（な）り立（た）つことを表（あらわ）します。そのため、(A) の事実（じじつ）を認（みと）めた上（うえ）で、別（べつ）の話題（わだい） (B) を述（の）べることができます。それに対（たい）して、「としても」（別（べつ）の文法事項（ぶんぽうじこう）で扱（あつか）います）は、「(A) と仮定（かてい）しても、(B) と判断（はんだん）できる」という表現（ひょうげん）です。「としても」では、(A) が (B) を生（う）み出（だ）す原因（げんいん）や条件（じょうけん）になっています。
attributes.body:
In the same way that にしては highlights a point to be considered about (A), or simply 'while (A)', the replacement of は with the adverbial particle も will put further emphasis on (B) being a surprising or unexpected thing that accompanies (A). This continues to reflect the case marking particle に's use as a location.

にしても may be translated as 'even considering (A), (B)', or 'even while (A), (B)', and may be used with any word in its plain form. にして by itself is often considered as a stand-alone adverbial particle, despite stemming from several parts.

にしても is very regularly used with Japanese's equivalent of WH-words, like どこ, どの, だれ, なに, etc. In these cases, it highlights that 'even considering (A) is undetermined (in location, number, amount, etc), (B)'.

Caution

As opposed to としても, a grammar point that will be covered in another lesson, にしても may introduce new topics (としても may not). This is due to にしても implying that (A) and (B) exist simultaneously, without the need for (B) to necessarily stem from (A). However, としても will always imply that (B) stems from (A) in some way.

attributes.description: The difference between としても and にしても
～にしても・～にしたって・～にしろ・～にせよ

attributes.body: Both ～と言っても and にしても can be translated as 'even though' or 'even if', but they differ in nuance. ～と言っても is used to downplay or soften expectations, e.g. 運動と言ってもウォーキング程度です ('Even though I say exercise, it's just walking'), while にしても has the nuance of 'even considering (A), (B)' or 'no matter if (A), (B)', e.g. 忙しいにしても連絡してほしい ('Even if they're busy, I'd at least like to be contacted').

attributes.body: Both どんなに〜ても and にしても introduce conditions contrary to results, but with different focuses. どんなに〜ても emphasizes an unchanging outcome despite extreme conditions, e.g. どんなに高くても買います ('I'll buy it no matter how expensive it is'), while にしても is used more flexibly to acknowledge a point while suggesting a contrast or reservation, e.g. 行くにしても、今日は無理だ ('Even if I go, today's not possible').

second_relatable.title: にしても
second_relatable.meaning: Even though, Even if, Even when, Also

attributes.body: にしても and にしろ～にしろ are similar in that both express 'whether', but にしても tends to focus on a single case and convey contrast or concession, e.g. 遅れるにしても連絡はしてほしい ('Even if you're late, I want you to contact me'). にしろ～にしろ pairs two options and stresses that the result remains the same, e.g. 勝つにしろ負けるにしろ ('Whether we win or lose').

first_relatable.title: にしても
first_relatable.meaning: Even though, Even if, Even when, Also

attributes.body: にしても and たとえ〜ても both mean 'even if', but にしても leans toward conditions that are reasonably likely, e.g. 難しいにしてもやってみたほうがいい ('Even if it's difficult, you should give it a try'). たとえ〜ても is far more hypothetical, e.g. たとえ失敗してもあきらめない ('Even if I fail, I won't give up').

attributes.body: にしても and としても both mean 'even if', but にしても can introduce a judgment that doesn't directly follow from the condition, e.g. 行くにしても不安だ ('Even if I go, I'm uneasy'). としても implies that the result stems logically from the assumption, e.g. 行くとしても一度だけだ ('Even if I go, it'll be only once').

attributes.body: にしても and ながらも both express contrast. にしても introduces something counter to the condition, e.g. 難しいにしてもやってみたほうがいい ('Even if it's hard, you should try doing it'). ながらも shows two opposing facts that coexist, e.g. 忙しいながらも楽しんでいる ('I'm busy, but still enjoying it').

attributes.body: にしても and にせよ・にしろ both mean 'even if' or 'regardless of', but にせよ・にしろ are stronger and more formal, often used in instruction or insistence, e.g. 行くにせよ行かないにせよ連絡してほしい ('Whether you go or not, I want you to let me know'). にしても is softer and more reflective, e.g. どこに行くにしても携帯は持っていったほうがいい ('Regardless of where you go, you should bring your cell phone').

attributes.body: にしても and たって are related in that たって is a more casual form of ても, meaning 'even if'. にしても could be rephrased as にしたって, which sounds more informal and emotional. For example, どこに行くにしても ('No matter where you go') can also be expressed as どこ行くにしたって.

attributes.body: にしても and とも both express 'even if', but differ in formality and structure. にしても follows the plain, non-past form and is more common in daily language, e.g. どこに行くにしても ('No matter where you go'). とも follows the volitional form and is more formal and emphatic, often found in set expressions like 何があろうとも ('No matter what happens').

attributes.body: Both にしても and のに express contrast, but with different nuances. のに is a general contrastive expression, like 'although.' にしても often presents a hypothetical or assumed condition, followed by an unexpected result. Like other ～ても forms, it's commonly used with Wh-words, e.g. どこに行くにしても 'no matter where you go'.

attributes.body: 何しろ and にしても are similar in that both have a general sense of 'no matter' or 'regardless', they are used quite differently. 何しろ comes at the beginning of a sentence to express 'after all, (A)', while にしても follows a noun or phrase to specifically state 'even if (A), still (B)'.

second_relatable.title: にしても

attributes.body: にしても and てでも both express determination in hypothetical or extreme situations. にしても presents a condition with contrast or concession, e.g. 行くにしても気が進まない ('Even if I go, I don't feel like it'). てでも emphasizes doing something even if it requires an extreme measure, e.g. 会うためなら借金してでも行く ('I'd even go into debt just to see them').

second_relatable.title: てでも
second_relatable.meaning: Even if I have to, By any or all means, No matter what

attributes.body: Both forms can mean 'even if' or 'even though,' but differ in nuance. ても is more versatile and often appears in expressions like てもいい 'it's okay to (A)' for asking or giving permission. にしても carries a stronger hypothetical tone, like 'Even supposing that...' which ても alone doesn't necessarily convey. Both are used with question words, e.g. どこに行っても and どこに行くにしても 'no matter where you go', with the latter sounding more hypothetical.

second_relatable.title: にしても
second_relatable.meaning: Even though, Even if, Even when, Also

attributes.body: かどうか expresses binary uncertainty, like 'whether or not', as in 行くかどうか分からない ('I don't know whether or not they'll go.'). にしても adds a tone of concession or contrast, like 'even if'. For example, どこに行くにしても 'no matter where (you) go'. The former asks a yes/no-type question, the latter implies acceptance of a situation.
